claim: When you create a Spot request you can choose the interruption behavior (stop, hibernate or terminate); by default Amazon EC2 terminates Spot Instances when they are interrupted.
question: What does Amazon EC2 do to an interrupted Spot Instance if you do not choose an interruption behavior?

values.display: terminates the instance by default
values.spoken: by default an interrupted Spot Instance is terminated

values.display: you can specify the interruption behavior
values.spoken: you can choose stop, hibernate or terminate

evidence.quote: The default behavior is that Amazon EC2 terminates Spot Instances when they are interrupted.
When Amazon EC2 interrupts a Spot Instance, it terminates the instance by default, unless you specify a different interruption behavior, such as stop or hibernate.
When you create a Spot request, you can specify the interruption behavior. The following are the possible interruption behaviors:

claim: To have interrupted Spot Instances stopped instead of terminated, the Spot Instance request type must be persistent and the request cannot specify a launch group; for EC2 Fleet or Spot Fleet the request type must be maintain.
question: Which Spot request type is required for the stop interruption behavior?

values.display: The Spot Instance request type must be persistent
values.spoken: stop on interruption needs a persistent Spot request

values.display: the request type must be maintain
values.spoken: for a fleet the type must be maintain

values.display: You can't specify a launch group

qualifiers.scope: Spot Instances with the stop interruption behavior

evidence.quote: You can specify that Amazon EC2 stops your Spot Instances when they are interrupted. The Spot Instance request type must be `persistent`. You can't specify a launch group in the Spot Instance request. For EC2 Fleet or Spot Fleet, the request type must be `maintain`.

claim: Only Amazon EC2 can restart a Spot Instance that was stopped by an interruption; for a persistent request it restarts the instance when capacity is available in the same Availability Zone for the same instance type.
question: Who restarts a Spot Instance that was stopped by an interruption, and where?

values.display: Only Amazon EC2 can restart
values.spoken: only EC2 can restart an interrupted stopped Spot Instance

values.display: when capacity is available in the same Availability Zone
values.spoken: it comes back in the same Availability Zone and instance type

qualifiers.scope: interrupted Spot Instances with the stop behavior

evidence.quote: Only Amazon EC2 can restart an interrupted stopped Spot Instance.

For a Spot Instance launched by a `persistent` Spot Instance request: Amazon EC2 restarts the stopped instance when capacity is available in the same Availability Zone and for the same instance type as the stopped instance (the same launch specification must be used).

claim: Amazon EC2 can interrupt a Spot Instance for capacity (it needs the capacity back), for price (the Spot price is higher than your maximum price), or for constraints (a launch group or Availability Zone group that can no longer be met).
question: For which reasons can Amazon EC2 interrupt a Spot Instance?

values.display: Amazon EC2 can interrupt your Spot Instance when it needs it back
values.spoken: capacity: EC2 needs the capacity back

values.display: The Spot price is higher than your maximum price
values.spoken: price: the Spot price is above your maximum price

values.display: terminated as a group
values.spoken: constraints: a launch group is terminated together

evidence.quote: Amazon EC2 can interrupt your Spot Instance when it needs it back. EC2 reclaims your instance mainly to repurpose capacity, but it can also occur for other reasons such as host maintenance or hardware decommission.
The Spot price is higher than your maximum price.
If your Spot request includes a constraint such as a launch group or an Availability Zone group, the Spot Instances are terminated as a group when the constraint can no longer be met.

claim: If you specify a maximum price in a Spot request, your instances are interrupted more frequently than if you do not specify one.
question: What is the effect of setting a maximum price on a Spot request?

values.display: interrupted more frequently
values.spoken: a maximum price means more interruptions

values.display: than if you do not specify it
values.spoken: leaving the maximum price empty is better

evidence.quote: You can specify the maximum price in your Spot request. However, if you specify a maximum price, your instances will be interrupted more frequently than if you do not specify it.

claim: With no maximum price (the recommended setting), a Spot Instance launches at the current Spot price and the price never exceeds the On-Demand price; whatever maximum price you set, you are always charged the current Spot price.
question: What do you pay for a Spot Instance with and without a maximum price?

values.display: The price will never exceed the On-Demand price
values.spoken: without a maximum price you never pay more than On-Demand

values.display: you will always be charged the current Spot price
values.spoken: you always pay the current Spot price

values.display: No maximum price

evidence.quote: **No maximum price**: Your Spot Instance will launch at the current Spot price. The price will never exceed the On-Demand price. (Recommended)
Regardless of the maximum price you specify, you will always be charged the current Spot price.

claim: A maximum price below the current Spot price means the Spot Instance does not launch; after it is running, if the Spot price rises above your maximum price, Amazon EC2 interrupts the instance.
question: What happens when the Spot price is above your maximum price, before and after launch?

values.display: your Spot Instance will not launch
values.spoken: below the current Spot price it does not launch

values.display: Amazon EC2 interrupts your Spot Instance
values.spoken: if the price rises above your maximum, EC2 interrupts it

qualifiers.scope: Spot Instance request with a maximum price

evidence.quote: If you specify a maximum price that is less than the current Spot price, your Spot Instance will not launch.

If you specify a maximum price that is more than the current Spot price, your Spot Instance will launch and be charged at the current Spot price. After your Spot Instance is running, if the Spot price rises above your maximum price, Amazon EC2 interrupts your Spot Instance.

claim: A Spot capacity pool is a set of unused EC2 instances with the same instance type and Availability Zone.
question: What is a Spot capacity pool?

values.display: A set of unused EC2 instances
values.spoken: a pool is unused instances of one type in one Availability Zone

values.display: with the same instance type
values.spoken: same instance type, same Availability Zone

evidence.quote: *Spot capacity pool* – A set of unused EC2 instances with the same instance type (for example, `m5.large`) and Availability Zone.

claim: The Spot price of each instance type in each Availability Zone is set by Amazon EC2 and adjusted gradually based on the long-term supply of and demand for Spot Instances.
question: At what level is the Spot price set, and what moves it?

values.display: each instance type in each Availability Zone
values.spoken: there is one Spot price per instance type per Availability Zone

values.display: adjusted gradually
values.spoken: it moves gradually with long-term supply and demand

evidence.quote: The Spot price of each instance type in each Availability Zone is set by Amazon EC2, and is adjusted gradually based on the long-term supply of and demand for Spot Instances.

claim: A persistent Spot Instance request stays active until it expires or you cancel it; after an interruption, when capacity returns, the instance is started if stopped or resumed if hibernated, and if the instance is terminated the request is opened again and EC2 launches a new Spot Instance.
question: What happens to a persistent Spot request after its instance is interrupted or terminated?

values.display: remains active until it expires or you cancel it
values.spoken: a persistent request stays until it expires or is cancelled

values.display: the Spot Instance request is opened again
values.spoken: if the instance is terminated, the request opens again

evidence.quote: A persistent Spot Instance request remains active until it expires or you cancel it, even if the request is fulfilled. If capacity is not available, your Spot Instance is interrupted. After your instance is interrupted, when capacity becomes available again, the Spot Instance is started if stopped or resumed if hibernated.
If the Spot Instance is terminated (irrespective of whether the Spot Instance is in a stopped or running state), the Spot Instance request is opened again and Amazon EC2 launches a new Spot Instance.

claim: A one-time Spot Instance request remains active until Amazon EC2 launches the Spot Instance, the request expires, or you cancel it; if capacity is not available the Spot Instance is terminated and the request is closed.
question: When does a one-time Spot request end?

values.display: remains active until Amazon EC2 launches the Spot Instance
values.spoken: a one-time request ends once the instance launches

values.display: the Spot Instance request is closed
values.spoken: after an interruption the one-time request is closed

evidence.quote: A one-time Spot Instance request remains active until Amazon EC2 launches the Spot Instance, the request expires, or you cancel the request. If capacity is not available, your Spot Instance is terminated and the Spot Instance request is closed.

claim: You cannot enable termination protection for Spot Instances.
question: Can you enable termination protection on a Spot Instance?

values.display: You can't enable termination protection for Spot Instances
values.spoken: Spot Instances cannot have termination protection

values.display: you must be prepared for interruptions
values.spoken: plan for interruptions instead

evidence.quote: When you use Spot Instances, you must be prepared for interruptions. Amazon EC2 can interrupt your Spot Instance when the demand for Spot Instances rises or when the supply of Spot Instances decreases. When Amazon EC2 interrupts a Spot Instance, it provides a Spot Instance interruption notice, which gives the instance a two-minute warning before Amazon EC2 interrupts it. You can't enable termination protection for Spot Instances.

claim: A launch group in a Spot request tells Amazon EC2 to launch the set of Spot Instances only if it can launch them all, and if the Spot service must terminate one instance in the group it must terminate them all.
question: What does a launch group do in a Spot Instance request?

values.display: only if it can launch them all
values.spoken: a launch group launches all instances or none

values.display: it must terminate them all
values.spoken: and terminates them all together

evidence.quote: Specify a launch group in your Spot Instance request to tell Amazon EC2 to launch a set of Spot Instances only if it can launch them all. In addition, if the Spot service must terminate one of the instances in a launch group, it must terminate them all.

claim: A rebalance recommendation is a signal that a Spot Instance is at elevated risk of interruption; it can arrive sooner than the two-minute interruption notice, but it is not always sent first and can arrive together with the notice.
question: How does a rebalance recommendation differ from the Spot interruption notice?

values.display: at elevated risk of interruption
values.spoken: a rebalance recommendation warns of elevated interruption risk

values.display: The signal can arrive sooner
values.spoken: it can come before the two-minute notice

values.display: can arrive along with the two-minute interruption notice

evidence.quote: An EC2 instance *rebalance recommendation* is a signal that notifies you when a Spot Instance is at elevated risk of interruption. The signal can arrive sooner than the [two-minute Spot Instance interruption notice](spot-instance-termination-notices.md), giving you the opportunity to proactively manage the Spot Instance.

It is not always possible for Amazon EC2 to send the rebalance recommendation signal before the two-minute Spot Instance interruption notice. Therefore, the rebalance recommendation signal can arrive along with the two-minute interruption notice.

claim: Rebalance recommendations are made available as an EventBridge event and as an item in the instance metadata of the Spot Instance, and events are emitted on a best effort basis.
question: Where can you receive a Spot rebalance recommendation?

values.display: made available as a EventBridge event
values.spoken: you get it as an EventBridge event

values.display: as an item in the instance metadata
values.spoken: and in the instance metadata

values.display: emitted on a best effort basis

evidence.quote: Rebalance recommendations are made available as a EventBridge event and as an item in the [instance metadata](ec2-instance-metadata.md) on the Spot Instance. Events are emitted on a best effort basis.

claim: A Spot placement score indicates how likely a Spot request is to succeed in a Region or Availability Zone; it serves only as a recommendation and gives no guarantee of capacity or interruption risk.
question: What does a Spot placement score tell you, and does it guarantee capacity?

values.display: how likely it is that a Spot request will succeed
values.spoken: the score says how likely a Spot request is to succeed

values.display: serves only as a recommendation
values.spoken: it is only a recommendation, not a guarantee

evidence.quote: A Spot placement score indicates how likely it is that a Spot request will succeed in a Region or Availability Zone.
A Spot placement score does not provide any guarantees in terms of available capacity or risk of interruption. A Spot placement score serves only as a recommendation.

values.spoken: On-Demand returns an insufficient capacity error

qualifiers.scope: Spot Instances compared with On-Demand Instances
